doc.title: feat(drive): randomizeRange for drive sheets (#1830)
doc.body:
Split out of #1830. Blocker #1831 closed as [ADR-0083](https://github.com/rust-works/omni-dev/blob/main/docs/adrs/adr-0083.md).

## What

`randomizeRange` has no request type in `src/drive/sheets/`. Shuffles the row
order within a range randomly (server-side; the resulting order is not
caller-specified or predictable).

Proposed verb: `randomize-range` (15 chars).

## Gate — resolved

[ADR-0083](https://github.com/rust-works/omni-dev/blob/main/docs/adrs/adr-0083.md)
§3 initially placed `randomizeRange` under `sheets-write` alone, on a
values-only reading, but flagged (§5) that whether the server carries a
row's **formatting** along with it when reordering was an open question with
a pre-decided consequence: if verified true, the gate becomes the
**`sheets-write` + `sheets-structure` union**.

Live-verified 2026-09-22 against a probe sheet in `omni-dev-test`
(`sortRange` and `randomizeRange` both tested; findings below apply to
this issue's `randomizeRange`):

- **Formatting moves with the row** — the §5 trigger fires. Gate is the
  union of `sheets-write` and `sheets-structure`
  (`target_gate::resolve_all`, the shape `text-to-columns` took in #1867).
- **Notes and data-validation rules move with the row** too.
- **In-range formulas move with their row and have their relative
  references rewritten**, so each formula keeps pointing at its own row.
- **Cells in the same rows but outside the selected columns do not
  move** — confirms §3's record-decoupling caveat: a range narrower than
  its rows can silently detach a record's other columns.

(The already-merged `sort-range` (#1842) predates this measurement and
shipped under `sheets-write` alone; a fix-forward for it is filed as
#1870, out of scope for this issue.)

## `--dry-run`

Cannot preview the resulting order (server-side randomness, same class of
limitation `autoFill` has for different reasons). Reports the range being
reordered, states plainly that the current row order is not preserved, and
leads with the range-width-vs-sheet-width record-integrity caveat before
the smaller "references outside the range may see a different row's
value" caveat — never a cell's contents.

## Status

Plan and live-verification findings posted in comments below. Branch
`issue-1845-randomize-range`, rebased even with `main`. Implementation not
yet started.

comments.author: newhoggy
comments.body:
## Plan

State of play: the blocker #1831 closed as [ADR-0083](https://github.com/rust-works/omni-dev/blob/main/docs/adrs/adr-0083.md) (numbered 0083, not the 0082 predicted in #1831's own plan comment). Sort-range (#1842, PR #1866), auto-fill (#1840, PR #1862) and text-to-columns (#1843, PR #1867) are all merged, and sort-range is the near-exact template for this verb. This worktree currently sits 12 commits behind `main` and predates sort-range, so step 1 rebases before anything else. No other grid-mutation PR is open right now, so the tracker's two-at-a-time snapshot-collision rule isn't a live constraint.

### What ADR-0083 fixes for this verb
- **§3**: `randomizeRange` joins `sheets-write` alone, on the values-only reading — a permutation of the range's own cells is a strict special case of what a `sheets-write` grant already permits via `clear`+`write`.
- **§6, "nothing discarded" tier**: no `values` read in `--dry-run`. The preview names the range, leads with the range-width-vs-sheet's-allocated-width record-integrity caveat (a narrower selection can silently decouple a record's other columns), then the smaller "references outside the range may see a different row's value" caveat. Never a value, and never a claim of predicting the resulting order — it's server-side randomness.
- **§5**: `randomizeRange` (alongside `sortRange`) is explicitly named as a live-verification item for two open questions: whether the server carries a row's **formatting** with it when moved, and what happens to a **formula inside the range** (moved with its row, references rewritten or not, or left in place). If formatting moves, the ADR's fixed rule requires flipping the gate to **both** `sheets-write` and `sheets-structure` (the text-to-columns precedent, which hit exactly this). Sort-range shipped *without* doing this verification, so this issue is the first time it actually gets answered for the reorder pair — and if the answer is "yes, formatting moves," sort-range's gate needs the same fix as a follow-up.

### Steps

1. **Rebase onto `origin/main`** so `src/drive/sheets/sort_range.rs` and its CLI module are present to mirror.
2. **Wire type** in `src/drive/sheets/types.rs`: `RandomizeRangeRequest { range: GridRange }` plus a `BatchUpdateRequestItem::RandomizeRange` variant, doc comment citing ADR-0083 §3, and a serialization test asserting `{"randomizeRange":{"range":{...}}}`.
3. **Engine** `src/drive/sheets/randomize_range.rs` — a trimmed copy of `sort_range.rs` with the sort-spec machinery removed. Same options struct minus `sort_by`; same result shape (`WouldChange`/`Changed` carrying `range` + `width_warning`); same flow: A1 compose → `target_gate::resolve` on `SheetsWrite` → `spreadsheets.get` → bounded-range refusal → width warning → dry-run returns before any lease/batchUpdate → `LeasedWrite` + `conclude_native_leased_write` for the real run. Log operation `sheets-randomize-range`. Lift the `width_warning` helper out of `sort_range.rs` into a shared `grid_range` helper rather than duplicating it (mirrors how #1843 lifted `non_blank_locations`).
4. **Preview/output wording**: dry-run — "Would randomize the row order of {range} in {book}" plus "the resulting order is chosen by the server and cannot be previewed; the current row order will not be preserved." Real run — "Randomized the row order of {range}" plus the outside-references caveat. No cell contents ever.
5. **CLI** `src/cli/drive/sheets/randomize_range.rs`: `randomize-range <ID> --range <A1> [--sheet NAME] [--dry-run] [lease flag] [-o]`. Register `RandomizeRange` in `SheetsSubcommands` right after `SortRange`, `pub mod` in `src/drive/sheets.rs`. Verb name is 15 chars, well inside the 27-char cap.
6. **Live verification (ADR-0083 §5)** — the step sort-range skipped. Back up `~/.omni-dev/settings.json`, add a temporary `sheets-write`-only rule scoped to the `omni-dev-test` folder, build a sheet with a bold/coloured row and a relative formula inside the target range, randomize it, read back values/formatting, restore settings and md5-verify. Record both findings in `docs/drive.md`:
   - If formatting moves with rows → switch the gate to `target_gate::resolve_all` over both operations, update the `SheetsStructure` doc comment, and file a follow-up issue for sort-range (same defect, different verb).
   - Formula-movement finding → caveat wording only, doesn't move the gate.
7. **Docs/sync**: new `#### drive sheets randomize-range` section in `docs/drive.md` between sort-range and auto-fill; add the verb to the default-policy table's `sheets-write` row; extend `SheetsWrite`'s doc comment in `src/drive/write_gate.rs`; `CHANGELOG.md` Unreleased entry citing #1845 and ADR-0083 §§3, 5, 6.
8. **Tests**, mirroring sort-range's set: request JSON, CLI parse, dry-run makes no `values` read and no batchUpdate, real run sends one `randomizeRange` request, open-ended/unknown-sheet refusals, denied-gate attempt recording, all four lease refusals, every `describe_lines` arm, jsonl output. Then the `update-snapshots` skill for the help golden, and a local `cargo llvm-cov --lib` pass before trusting any posted PR coverage comment.
9. **Ship**: commit as `feat(drive): add sheets randomize-range command`, lint with `omni-dev git commit message lint origin/main..HEAD`, open a PR fixing #1845 citing ADR-0083 §§3, 5, 6, then tick the tracker checkbox in #1830.

### Calls made without asking
- Require a fully bounded range, same as sort-range (`A2:D100`, not `A:A`/`2:2`).
- No confirmation flag (ADR-0075 §3), consistent with the rest of the tranche.

### Flagged for visibility
If step 6's live verification finds that formatting moves with reordered rows, the scope grows beyond this issue alone: it changes this verb's gate to a two-operation composition *and* surfaces that sort-range (#1842, already merged) is mis-gated under the same rule, requiring a follow-up there. That's in-scope per ADR-0083 §5's own fixed rule, not a scope decision I'm making unilaterally.

comments.body:
## Residual resolved — live verification run before implementing

The plan above left one fork open (step 6: ADR-0083 §5's formatting/formula question). It has now been measured live rather than deferred to implementation time, by sending the real `sortRange` and `randomizeRange` requests to a probe sheet (`omni-dev #1845 reorder probe` in `omni-dev-test`, left in place) and reading the grid back with `includeGridData`.

Probe layout: A2:C6 with one bold+pink row, one row carrying a note, one cell with a data-validation rule, a relative formula per row in column C, plus an absolute and a relative reference in column D (same rows, outside the reordered columns) and a `=B2` reference from row 7 outside the range.

**Findings, identical for both requests:**

- **Formatting moves with the row.** That is §5's pre-decided trigger, so `randomize-range` gates on **both `sheets-write` and `sheets-structure`** (`target_gate::resolve_all`, the shape `text-to-columns` took in #1867). Not a fork any more.
- **Notes and data-validation rules move with the row** as well.
- **In-range formulas move with their row and their relative references are rewritten** (`=B3*2` became `=B2*2` once its row landed on row 2), so each formula keeps pointing at its own row. This fixes §6's caveat wording: the risk is not formulas *inside* the range, it is references *into* it from outside.
- **Cells in the same rows but outside the selected columns stay put** and now read a different record's value — §3's record-decoupling caveat, confirmed, and the reason the preview leads with the width warning.
- `randomizeRange` returns an empty reply; the real run reports what it sent.

**Plan amendments:**

- Step 3/6: gate is the two-operation union from the first commit; no conditional branch. `docs/drive.md`'s section records all four facts, and the `SheetsStructure` doc comment gains `randomize-range`.
- Step 7: the default-policy table lists `randomize-range` under both `sheets-write` and `sheets-structure` (as `text-to-columns` is), not under `sheets-write` alone.
- Step 8: add the union-gate test — a rule allowing `sheets-write` but explicitly denying `sheets-structure` yields `Blocked`.
- Sort-range is mis-gated by the same rule; filed as #1870 rather than widening this issue.

The routing signal's "design needs opus (close call)" was pointing at exactly this open fork. With it measured, what remains is implementation on a settled design.

doc.title: feat(jev): sharpen route's complexity-reduction signal (could_be_cheaper scope, citation relations, tier margins, spike detection)
doc.body:
## Summary

Four related gaps in `omni-dev ai jev route`'s ability to tell a reader *why* an issue
classified the way it did and *what would lower it*, found by using `route` against
issue #1845 during that issue's own triage (2026-09-22 — see that issue's comment
thread for the worked example this issue is built from):

1. **`could_be_cheaper` is design-stage only**, so it gives no signal when `implement`
   is the higher stage (`class = max(design, implement)`).
2. **Citation detection can't distinguish a real dependency from provenance.** `find_citations`
   treats "Blocked on #N" and "Split out of #N" identically, so a `could_be_cheaper`
   question gets asked about a parent tracker whose closure was never actually a
   precondition for the routed issue's own work.
3. **Text output hides the runner-up tier.** `Answer::Choice` already carries a full
   `probabilities` map; `render_stage_line`/`render_stage_clause` render only the
   winning choice and its confidence, so "close call" gives no sense of what it was
   close *to* without switching to `-o json`.
4. **No way to distinguish "needs judgment" from "needs a spike."** The `stage_design`
   question asks whether "the text already settles the approach and the open
   questions" — but an "open question" can mean two very different things: genuine
   unresolved judgment (needs a higher-tier model to think it through), or a single
   bounded, already-specified empirical test whose result mechanically selects between
   two already-decided branches (a spike). `route` currently scores both the same way.

## Motivation — the #1845 case

#1845 (`randomizeRange` for `drive sheets`) was routed while its design was gated on
one live-verification question from [ADR-0083](https://github.com/rust-works/omni-dev/blob/main/docs/adrs/adr-0083.md)
§5: does the Sheets API carry a row's formatting along with it when reordering? The
ADR had *already* pre-decided the consequence either way — if yes, gate on both
`sheets-write` and `sheets-structure`; if no, `sheets-write` alone — so the only
remaining work was running the test and applying the rule its answer selected. No
further architectural judgment was needed.

`route` classified `design` as `opus`, confidence 0.18, "close call" — reasonable
given what it could see (item 4: the issue's own text, and the ADR it linked to but
`build_route_state` deliberately excludes for token cost, read as an unresolved open
question with no way to tell it apart from a genuinely hard one), but not actually
telling the operator "the way to lower this is to spend 20 minutes on one bounded API
probe," which is what running it actually was. The `depends_on` line the same run
produced (`cites open #1830, which could leave less design work if resolved (0.43)`)
pointed at the tracker issue #1845 was split out of, which was never itself a
precondition for closing this issue's design fork — items 1 and 2 above.

## Proposed changes

### 1. Extend `could_be_cheaper` to the `implement` stage

Same mechanism #1812 shipped for `design` (`could_be_cheaper_question` in
`src/jev/route.rs`), asked a second time per open citation, keyed
`could_be_cheaper.implement` in the report. #1812's own Open Questions section already
flagged this as deferred, not abandoned, for exactly this reason (rust-works/succinctly#2063 in that
issue's evidence was a citation whose real bearing was on `implement`, untested at the
time). Needs the same live-evidence validation round #1812 ran for `design` before the
wording ships — not done as part of this issue.

### 2. Relation-aware citation weighting

Recognize "blocked on"/"blocks"/"depends on"/"requires" phrasing near a citation as a
stronger dependency signal than a bare `#N` or "split from"/"tracker"/"split out of"
phrasing, and either suppress `could_be_cheaper` for the weak-signal case or label it
distinctly in the report (`relation: "tracker"` vs `relation: "blocker"`) so a reader
can discount it themselves. The cheaper version of this — labeling rather than
suppressing — avoids guessing wrong and hiding a real dependency; suppressing outright
is riskier and would need its own evidence round given #1812's Round 1 finding that
even Jev-driven signals here get fooled by how the citing sentence is actually worded.

### 3. Show the runner-up tier in text output

`render_stage_clause`/`render_stage_line` (`src/jev/route.rs`) already have
`answer.probabilities` on hand (`Answer::Choice`'s full distribution from Jev); add
the second-highest tier and its probability to the close-call case only, e.g.
`opus (0.18, close call — sonnet 0.16)`. Pure rendering change, no new Jev call, no
wording to validate — lowest-cost item here and shippable without an evidence round.

### 4. A spike-vs-judgment signal

The most novel and least validated item. Proposed as a new `noul` question per
routed issue (not per citation, since it's about the issue's own text rather than a
cross-reference): something like *"does the remaining design work reduce to running
one specific, already-named test or experiment whose result has an already-stated
consequence for each outcome, rather than requiring further judgment to decide what to
do?"* A high answer would let `route` report e.g. `sonnet — pending one bounded spike`
instead of folding a spike indistinguishably into the stage tier. Needs the same kind
of live round #1812 ran for `could_be_cheaper` (redacted/simulated-resolved text,
checked against a human reading, checked for confounds) before the wording is trusted
— explicitly **not** done here; this issue proposes the direction, not validated
wording.

## Non-goals

- Not feeding an issue's linked ADR content into the existing stage questions —
  `docs/jev.md` already documents that feeding cross-issue content in made routing
  *worse* (#1812's Motivation section, agreement 12/16 → 9/16). Item 4 is deliberately
  a separate, narrowly-scoped question rather than widening what the stage questions
  see.
- Not auto-detecting spikes by keyword matching ("TODO: verify", "unknown", etc.) —
  too easy to both false-positive on hedging language and false-negative on a spike
  described without those words. If item 4 ships, it goes through Jev like
  `could_be_cheaper` does, not a local heuristic.

## Open questions & caveats

- Items 1, 2 and 4 all need a live-evidence validation round against real issues
  before any wording ships, per this project's own standard for Jev question wording
  (every question here — the stage questions, `verify-decision`'s splitter,
  `could_be_cheaper` itself — has been bitten by an unvalidated first draft at least
  once; see #1812's Evidence section for the shape that validation takes). None of
  that validation work is done in this issue; it's a design proposal built from one
  worked case (#1845), not measured evidence.
- Item 3 is the exception: it needs no validation, since it renders data Jev already
  returns rather than asking a new question. Cheapest to ship, and could land ahead of
  the rest.
- Item 2's suppress-vs-label choice is an open question in itself, not resolved here.

## Implementation plan

### 1. Ship the runner-up display independently

- Add one shared stage-answer formatter used by both the compact
  `render_stage_clause` and multiline `render_stage_line` paths. For a stage in
  `close_calls`, show the highest-probability **nonchosen** option and its
  probability, e.g. `opus (0.18, close call — sonnet 0.16)`. Keep the chosen
  answer's existing `confidence` value distinct from the alternatives in
  `probabilities`.
- Pick deterministically when probabilities tie (option name as a stable
  tiebreaker). If Jev provides no usable alternative, retain `close call`
  without inventing a runner-up. Include `none` when it is a genuine design
  alternative and support custom and multi-model tier names.
- Test close and non-close calls in both text layouts, ties, absent
  alternatives, and a multi-ladder report. Keep the JSON schema and Jev
  request unchanged. Update the text-output example in `docs/jev.md`.

### 2. Establish evidence before changing Jev signals

- Assemble a small, documented set of real open issues and citations with a
  human reading recorded before looking at Jev's new answers. Cover real
  blockers, parent trackers/provenance, ambiguous wording, implementation-led
  class choices, bounded experiments with pre-decided branches, and open
  design questions that still require judgment. Include #1845/#1830, but do
  not tune wording to that one pair.
- For each candidate question, record the exact input text, question wording,
  Jev model/version, response, token cost, expected reading, and failures.
  Compare against the existing route result, a redacted-citation or
  simulated-resolved variant where applicable, and a manual reading. Check
  whether adding questions to the same Jev request changes the existing
  stage answers. Repeat ambiguous cases to expose instability.
- Keep linked ADR and other cross-issue content out of `build_route_state`.
  In particular, if #1845's own text does not state both consequences of its
  proposed test, a low or uncertain spike answer is appropriate; a question
  cannot recover facts that were never sent to Jev. Record that limit rather
  than silently broadening the input.
- Do not ship new question wording solely because it fits #1845. Publish the
  cases, observed mismatches, and the final wording in `docs/jev.md`, as was
  done for #1812.

### 3. Add implementation-stage `could_be_cheaper`

- After its wording passes step 2, ask one additional `noul` question per
  open citation about **this issue's remaining implementation work**. Keep
  the existing, validated design wording byte-for-byte; key the two answers
  separately and ask each once per citation, regardless of the number of
  provider ladders.
- Populate `could_be_cheaper: {design: ..., implement: ...}`. Treat missing or
  malformed answers independently: retain the citation and any valid stage
  score, logging the missing answer; omit the entry only when neither score
  is available. Render both scores with explicit stage names so the reader
  can see which stage could get cheaper.
- Test request keys, answer extraction, partial answers, several citations,
  one versus several ladders, JSON serialization, and text output. Document
  that these scores describe possible remaining work, not a recalculated
  route class.

### 4. Label citation relations conservatively

- Prefer labeling over suppressing. Expose a `relation` value such as
  `blocker`, `tracker`, or `unspecified` on each open citation and show it in
  text output. Keep all open citations visible; do not use the label to
  change stage choices or `could_be_cheaper` scores.
- Preserve enough nearby wording for route-specific relation assessment.
  `find_citations` currently deduplicates by target and keeps only the first
  raw match, which can lose a later explicit dependency statement. Handle
  repeated mentions of the same target and sentence scope, including
  negation and quoted text. Keep `verify-decision`'s citation resolution and
  boundary behavior intact.
- Validate proposed relation rules against the step-2 cases before fixing
  them. Use `unspecified` when the text does not support a stronger claim.
  Test blocker, tracker, neutral, conflicting and repeated mentions, and
  ensure the #1845 parent tracker is not presented as a proven blocker.

### 5. Add a bounded-spike signal

- After validating the wording, add one issue-level `noul` question, not one
  per citation or provider ladder. It should score whether a **specific,
  bounded empirical test** remains and the action for each possible result
  is already stated in the routed issue's text. A named test with undecided
  consequences must not count as a settled fork.
- Add the result as a separate explanation in structured and text output.
  Do not silently lower `stage_design`, `class`, or a provider tier based on
  this score. Choose any high-score label or display threshold from the
  validation results rather than an arbitrary first draft.
- Test one question per issue, absence/partial answers, high and low cases,
  and preservation of the existing stage results. Document what the signal
  does and what missing linked context prevents it from knowing.

### Release checks

- Land step 1 separately if useful; gate steps 3–5 on the recorded live
  evidence in step 2. The relation schema and final spike wording remain
  subject to those results.
- Run focused Rust tests, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`,
  `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and the applicable full test
  suite from this worktree. Review example output and JSON/YAML compatibility.
  Update `docs/jev.md` and `CHANGELOG.md` for shipped behavior.

comments.body:
## First uncertainty-reduction pass (2026-09-22)

### What is ready

Item 3 (runner-up in text output) is implemented in PR #1873. It changes only rendering, with no new Jev question. Focused route tests (88), formatting, Clippy, build, and a live #1871 text-output run passed. The live result included `design needs no further work (0.21, close call — sol 0.39)`.

### The current route choice is unstable near `none`/`sol`

The reported run above chose `sol` for design (confidence 0.21). Three further identical `jev-1.13.0` runs on #1871 using the OpenAI ladder chose `none` (confidence 0.34, 0.24, 0.26). Their `P(none)`/`P(sol)` pairs were 0.50/0.34, 0.43/0.39 and 0.45/0.37. The post-build live smoke run also chose `none` (confidence 0.21, runner-up `sol` 0.39). This is a close boundary, not evidence that editing the plan definitively removed all design work. The OpenAI ladder itself remains unvalidated as documented in `docs/jev.md`.

### Candidate implementation-stage question: preliminary, do not ship yet

I tested a direct adaptation of the existing design `could_be_cheaper` question against current issue text (title, body, comments), with Jev pinned to `jev-1.13.0`. It asks whether resolving the citation would leave less implementation work for **this** issue, assuming design is already done. Human readings were set before looking at the scores.

| Routed issue → citation | Prior reading | `could_be_cheaper.implement` |
|---|---|---:|
| rust-works/succinctly#1356 → rust-works/succinctly#1129 | Explicit blocker; implementation bearing plausible | 0.47 |
| rust-works/succinctly#1343 → rust-works/succinctly#2063 | Implementation-only caveat; modest bearing | 0.51 |
| rust-works/succinctly#1998 → rust-works/succinctly#1419 | Parallel/sibling scope; low bearing | 0.39 |
| rust-works/succinctly#1740 → rust-works/succinctly#1753 | Work absorbed by the cited issue; high bearing | 0.82 |
| omni-dev#1845 → #1830 | Parent tracker, not a blocker | 0.32 |
| omni-dev#1871 → #1845 | Worked-example provenance, not a blocker | 0.23 |

The absorbed case separates clearly, but the middle scores overlap. These are single runs on current text, not the resolved-simulation check used in #1812 or forward validation. In particular, rust-works/succinctly#1356's explicit blocker only scored 0.47. Keep the implementation question out of the product until the simulated-resolved comparison and repeated ambiguous cases are done. The exact candidate question was:

> This issue cites `<CITATION>`, which is still open. If `<CITATION>` is resolved, how likely is it that LESS implementation work (code, tests and docs) would remain for THIS issue than the current text implies — as opposed to this issue own remaining implementation work being unaffected because it is already scoped separately, is a parallel or sibling effort, or `<CITATION>` is otherwise not a precondition for finishing this issue own remaining work? Assume any remaining design work has been completed well.

### Candidate spike question: scope matters

I compared three `noul` wordings. The #1845 "pre-probe" state was reconstructed from its first plan comment without the later resolution; it is **not** an exact archived route input. #1843's pre-probe state used its body and first plan comment. The current/resolved cases used today's title, body and comments. All calls used `jev-1.13.0`.

| Input | Strict "remaining design reduces to one test" | Broad "has a pending test" | Own-issue pending-fork wording |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| #1845 pre-probe plan | 0.33 | 0.94 | 0.90 (repeat 0.89) |
| #1845 after probe | 0.19 | 0.24 | 0.11 |
| #1871 (describes #1845 as an example) | 0.16 | **0.78 false positive** | 0.06 (repeat 0.06) |
| rust-works/succinctly#1998 | 0.06 | 0.18 | 0.20 |
| #1843 pre-probe plan | not run | not run | 0.82 |

The strict question missed the historical #1845 case. The broad question confused #1871's worked example with a spike in #1871's own work. The own-issue wording avoided that confound in this small set. #1843 also still had a separate judgment call, so a high result can only mean **a bounded spike exists**; it must not claim that all design work is gone or lower the chosen tier.

The tested own-issue wording was:

> For THIS issue's own remaining design work (not a worked example, quoted case, cited issue, or proposed feature), is there a specific empirical check that has not yet been run and for which THIS issue already states the concrete action to take for each relevant result? Score high only if performing that check directly settles a live design fork in THIS issue without further architectural judgment. Score low if the check is already complete, merely an example, or additional design judgment is still needed.

This is a promising candidate, not ship-ready wording. It still needs more real positive and negative issues, a batched-question drift check against the existing stage answers, and human review of false positives before choosing a display threshold.

### Citation relation decision

Choose **labeling, not suppression**: keep every open citation visible, with `blocker`, `tracker`, or `unspecified` only when the citing context supports that label. Hiding a genuine dependency is a worse failure than showing an `unspecified` reference. A parent tracker such as #1845→#1830 should not be described as a blocker; #1871→#1845 is example provenance and should stay `unspecified` unless a more precise label earns its own evidence. Before implementation, test repeated references (the current scanner keeps only the first), sentence scope, negation and quoted text against real issues. No local keyword rule is approved by these six cases alone.

### Remaining gates

1. Compare implementation-stage scores with hand-edited resolved simulations, repeat borderline cases, and check the effect of batching the new question with stage questions.

doc.title: yq: YamlValue::key_string's "" fallback would collapse two different keys under jq-mode collapse
doc.body:
**Severity: Low** (latent, not currently reachable) — noted while working #1642, not filed
at the time.

## Summary

`YamlValue::key_string()` (`src/yaml/light.rs:6154-6169`) returns the literal empty string
`""` for any key with no scalar form — a complex/non-scalar key (issue #222), and, since
#1642, a key whose bytes fail to *decode* too (`document::key_display_string` falls back to
`Cow::Borrowed("")` for any `DocumentValue` whose `key_raw_source_span()` is `None`, which
it always is for YAML — there is no raw-span concept there, unlike JSON).

The identity/collapse machinery that decides whether two fields share a name for jq-mode's
duplicate-key-collapses rule (`collapse_repeated`/`collapse_confirmed_repeat`/
`DistinctKeyCursors` in `src/jq/document.rs`) keys off `key_string()`/`key_hash_of()`
directly. If **two different** such YAML keys in one mapping both stringify to `""` (e.g.
two distinct complex keys, or two different-but-both-undecodable scalar keys), and this
mapping were ever evaluated under `S::COLLAPSE_DUPLICATE_KEYS = true` (`JqSemantics`),
the collapse machinery would treat both `""`-keyed fields as *the same* key and silently
collapse them to one — the exact class of bug #1642 fixed for JSON's analogous case
(`key_hash_of`/`DistinctKeyCursors` staying `None`-safe for a JSON decode-failure key was
the fix's whole point; YAML's `""` convention sidesteps `None` entirely by always
succeeding, which is safe only because nothing collapses it today).

## Why this is not live today

Confirmed by reading the call graph, not by reproducing a failure: `YamlValue` is only ever
evaluated under `YqSemantics` (`COLLAPSE_DUPLICATE_KEYS = false`) in the shipped binary.
`src/bin/succinctly/jq_runner.rs` never references `YamlValue`/`YamlIndex` at all, and
`yq_runner.rs`'s own `--input-format json` bridge (`to_owned_canonicalizing_numbers`,
added alongside #1642's fix) pairs `StandardJson` with `YqSemantics` — the *other*
direction, JSON read but evaluated in yq mode, not YAML read but evaluated in jq mode. So
there is no live path today that pairs `YamlValue` with `JqSemantics`, and this is
currently unreachable.

## Suggested direction (not attempted)

Either:
1. Give `YamlValue` its own `key_raw_source_span` in the same spirit as JSON's (a raw
   scalar-node byte span, when one exists) so a decode-failure YAML key gets a
   distinguishing fallback instead of a shared `""` — closing the gap the same way #1642
   closed it for JSON, symmetric across formats even though only one side is reachable
   today; or
2. Leave `""` as-is (matching the pre-existing #222 convention for genuinely complex keys,
   which has the identical property) and instead assert in code — a debug assertion or a
   type-level constraint — that `YamlValue` and `JqSemantics` are never paired, so a future
   change that introduces such a pairing fails loudly instead of silently reintroducing
   this class of bug.

## Related

- #1642 — the JSON-side fix this gap mirrors; see its "YAML" section in the PR/commit
  history for the original context this was noted in.
- #222 — established the `""` convention for a YAML key with no scalar form, which this
  issue's collision risk is really about (the decode-failure case just widened how often
  the convention fires).

comments.author: newhoggy
comments.body:
## Triage (2026-09-04) — absorbed by #1753; neither suggested option

Still latent: `jq_runner.rs` never touches `YamlValue`, and `yq_runner.rs` only uses `JqSemantics` for
`to_json_for_reindex` on an `OwnedValue`. But option 2 is not available — `eval_generic::eval_using` is
`pub` and `test_yaml_generic_to_entries_collapses_under_jq_semantics_1385` deliberately pins the
`YamlValue`+`JqSemantics` pairing as supported library surface. Option 1 (a YAML raw span) is moot.

**Decision.** Fix it inside #1753: `key_hash_of` (`src/jq/document.rs`) returns `None` when
`key.key_is_complex()`, the same "never a duplicate" answer it already gives a decode-failure key, so
`DistinctKeyCursors`/`collapse_repeated` never merge two complex keys under `COLLAPSE_DUPLICATE_KEYS = true`.
Pin with a unit test beside the 1385 one: `? {}: 1 / ? []: 2` under `eval_using::<JqSemantics, _>(to_entries)`
→ two entries. Close with #1753.

doc.title: feat(drive): randomizeRange for drive sheets (#1830)
doc.body:
## Plan

State of play: the blocker #1831 closed as [ADR-0083](https://github.com/rust-works/omni-dev/blob/main/docs/adrs/adr-0083.md) (numbered 0083, not the 0082 predicted in #1831's own plan comment). Sort-range (#1842, PR #1866), auto-fill (#1840, PR #1862) and text-to-columns (#1843, PR #1867) are all merged, and sort-range is the near-exact template for this verb. This worktree currently sits 12 commits behind `main` and predates sort-range, so step 1 rebases before anything else. No other grid-mutation PR is open right now, so the tracker's two-at-a-time snapshot-collision rule isn't a live constraint.

### What ADR-0083 fixes for this verb
- **§3**: `randomizeRange` joins `sheets-write` alone, on the values-only reading — a permutation of the range's own cells is a strict special case of what a `sheets-write` grant already permits via `clear`+`write`.
- **§6, "nothing discarded" tier**: no `values` read in `--dry-run`. The preview names the range, leads with the range-width-vs-sheet's-allocated-width record-integrity caveat (a narrower selection can silently decouple a record's other columns), then the smaller "references outside the range may see a different row's value" caveat. Never a value, and never a claim of predicting the resulting order — it's server-side randomness.
- **§5**: `randomizeRange` (alongside `sortRange`) is explicitly named as a live-verification item for two open questions: whether the server carries a row's **formatting** with it when moved, and what happens to a **formula inside the range** (moved with its row, references rewritten or not, or left in place). If formatting moves, the ADR's fixed rule requires flipping the gate to **both** `sheets-write` and `sheets-structure` (the text-to-columns precedent, which hit exactly this). Sort-range shipped *without* doing this verification, so this issue is the first time it actually gets answered for the reorder pair — and if the answer is "yes, formatting moves," sort-range's gate needs the same fix as a follow-up.

### Steps

1. **Rebase onto `origin/main`** so `src/drive/sheets/sort_range.rs` and its CLI module are present to mirror.
2. **Wire type** in `src/drive/sheets/types.rs`: `RandomizeRangeRequest { range: GridRange }` plus a `BatchUpdateRequestItem::RandomizeRange` variant, doc comment citing ADR-0083 §3, and a serialization test asserting `{"randomizeRange":{"range":{...}}}`.
3. **Engine** `src/drive/sheets/randomize_range.rs` — a trimmed copy of `sort_range.rs` with the sort-spec machinery removed. Same options struct minus `sort_by`; same result shape (`WouldChange`/`Changed` carrying `range` + `width_warning`); same flow: A1 compose → `target_gate::resolve` on `SheetsWrite` → `spreadsheets.get` → bounded-range refusal → width warning → dry-run returns before any lease/batchUpdate → `LeasedWrite` + `conclude_native_leased_write` for the real run. Log operation `sheets-randomize-range`. Lift the `width_warning` helper out of `sort_range.rs` into a shared `grid_range` helper rather than duplicating it (mirrors how #1843 lifted `non_blank_locations`).
4. **Preview/output wording**: dry-run — "Would randomize the row order of {range} in {book}" plus "the resulting order is chosen by the server and cannot be previewed; the current row order will not be preserved." Real run — "Randomized the row order of {range}" plus the outside-references caveat. No cell contents ever.
5. **CLI** `src/cli/drive/sheets/randomize_range.rs`: `randomize-range <ID> --range <A1> [--sheet NAME] [--dry-run] [lease flag] [-o]`. Register `RandomizeRange` in `SheetsSubcommands` right after `SortRange`, `pub mod` in `src/drive/sheets.rs`. Verb name is 15 chars, well inside the 27-char cap.
6. **Live verification (ADR-0083 §5)** — the step sort-range skipped. Back up `~/.omni-dev/settings.json`, add a temporary `sheets-write`-only rule scoped to the `omni-dev-test` folder, build a sheet with a bold/coloured row and a relative formula inside the target range, randomize it, read back values/formatting, restore settings and md5-verify. Record both findings in `docs/drive.md`:
   - If formatting moves with rows → switch the gate to `target_gate::resolve_all` over both operations, update the `SheetsStructure` doc comment, and file a follow-up issue for sort-range (same defect, different verb).
   - Formula-movement finding → caveat wording only, doesn't move the gate.
7. **Docs/sync**: new `#### drive sheets randomize-range` section in `docs/drive.md` between sort-range and auto-fill; add the verb to the default-policy table's `sheets-write` row; extend `SheetsWrite`'s doc comment in `src/drive/write_gate.rs`; `CHANGELOG.md` Unreleased entry citing #1845 and ADR-0083 §§3, 5, 6.
8. **Tests**, mirroring sort-range's set: request JSON, CLI parse, dry-run makes no `values` read and no batchUpdate, real run sends one `randomizeRange` request, open-ended/unknown-sheet refusals, denied-gate attempt recording, all four lease refusals, every `describe_lines` arm, jsonl output. Then the `update-snapshots` skill for the help golden, and a local `cargo llvm-cov --lib` pass before trusting any posted PR coverage comment.
9. **Ship**: commit as `feat(drive): add sheets randomize-range command`, lint with `omni-dev git commit message lint origin/main..HEAD`, open a PR fixing #1845 citing ADR-0083 §§3, 5, 6, then tick the tracker checkbox in #1830.

### Calls made without asking
- Require a fully bounded range, same as sort-range (`A2:D100`, not `A:A`/`2:2`).
- No confirmation flag (ADR-0075 §3), consistent with the rest of the tranche.

### Flagged for visibility
If step 6's live verification finds that formatting moves with reordered rows, the scope grows beyond this issue alone: it changes this verb's gate to a two-operation composition *and* surfaces that sort-range (#1842, already merged) is mis-gated under the same rule, requiring a follow-up there. That's in-scope per ADR-0083 §5's own fixed rule, not a scope decision I'm making unilaterally.

doc.title: perf(jq): re-measure the walk's remaining double position-resolve now that path/key/parent/getpath are off it (#2168 Stage 2)
doc.body:
**Severity: Low** (perf only; no incorrect output). Carried over from #2168, which is now closed.

## What

#2168's own investigation found the cursor walk resolves each node's `text_position` two
to three times per node: once in `uncons`, again in the delimiter/gap checks, and again
in `c.value()` on recursion. #2578 (direction 1) fixed the *seed* `text_position` gallops
from, which recovered most of the per-lookup cost regardless of how many times a node's
position gets resolved. #2604 (direction 2) removed the walk entirely for `path`, `key`,
`parent` and `getpath` — the shapes #2168 was filed about.

What is left running the walk is `select`, the `sort_by`/`unique_by`/`min_by`/`max_by`
family, and `to_owned_cursor_at_depth` — because for those, the subtree walked *is* the
value tested or materialized, not a bounded navigation (see #2604's rationale in
`docs/compliance/jq/limitations.md`). #2168's closing comment on the merged PR says this
narrower remainder is "worth re-measuring against what is left before anyone commits to
it" — with the seed fix and the four-builtin carve-out both in, the double-resolve may no
longer be worth fixing, or may still be a real cost on `select`/`sort_by`-shaped queries
over large documents. Nobody has re-run the numbers since #2604 landed.

## Why file this now

The note that raised it only exists in a comment on #2168, which is now **closed** — so it
won't surface in an open-issue triage, and the actual next step (re-measure, then decide)
was never captured as its own actionable item.

## Suggested approach

Not prescribing a fix. First step is the re-measurement #2168 asked for: A/B `select(f)`
and `sort_by(f)`-shaped queries (large document, condition/key touching most or all of the
subtree) against the current `main`, now that #2578's seed and #2604's carve-out are both
in, and see whether the double-resolve is still a visible fraction of the remaining cost
before deciding whether a fusion pass is worth it.

## Related

- #2168 — where this was originally raised and where the "worth re-measuring" note lives.
- #2578 — the seed fix that already recovered most of the per-lookup cost this issue is about.
- #2604 — removed the walk entirely for `path`/`key`/`parent`/`getpath`, narrowing this
  issue's remaining scope to `select`/`sort_by` family/`to_owned_cursor_at_depth`.

comments.author: newhoggy
comments.body:
## Triage plan (2026-09-12)

**Premise check on current `main` (`2581b17c9`):** partially holds, and the remaining scope has shrunk again since filing. Not re-measured here (benchmarks deliberately not run during triage); this is a code-reading check of what still runs the walk and what a second resolve of the same node now costs.

- `select`/`if` are **off the walk entirely** since #2692 (`dd960f893`, 2026-09-10, one day after this issue was filed): `push_generic_truthiness` now tests `DocumentCursor::is_falsy`, O(1), and `push_generic_document_validation_error`'s only surviving caller is `key_elements_generic` (`src/jq/eval_generic.rs`) for the `_by` forms — `sort_by`/`unique_by`/`min_by`/`max_by`/`group_by`. The bare `sort`/`unique`/`min`/`max` forms go through `to_owned_cursor`, as does every other materialization (`[.[]]`, `tojson`, `-S`, the wildcard bridge).
- The "two to three resolves per node" is real but no longer costs two to three gallops. In `to_owned_cursor_at_depth`'s array arm the sequence per element is `element_gap_ok(is_first)` (resolves `text_position`) then the recursive call's `cursor.value()` (resolves it again); in the object arm `checked_key` → `delimiters_ok` → `key_delimiter_ok`/`value_delimiter_ok` resolve the key's and value's positions, then the recursion resolves the value's again; `container_tail_gap_ok` re-asks the last child once after the loop. But #2578 gave `JsonIndex::ib_select1_sequential` (`src/json/light.rs`) an **exact-repeat fast path** — `k == last.rank` answers from the `seq_hint` cell without probing, and its doc comment names this very pattern ("`DocumentCursor` callers routinely ask the same node twice (`text_position()` then `value()`)"); YAML's `AdvancePositions` has the same `last_ib_arg` short-circuit (`src/yaml/advance_positions.rs`). So the second resolve of a node now costs one `BalancedParens::rank1` (an L1/L2 table lookup plus a popcount) plus the compare — not a select gallop. The only asks that still probe are the genuinely distinct ones (key then value) and the backward tail re-ask, which the extrapolated seed lands within a word or two of.
- In JSON, `uncons`/`uncons_cursor` do not resolve positions at all (BP navigation only), so the issue's "once in `uncons`" is not a term on the JSON side.

**Root cause / mechanism:** the walk's structure asks each node's position from two or three separate helpers (`element_gap_ok`, `key_delimiter_ok`/`value_delimiter_ok`, `value()`) instead of resolving once and threading `pos` down, the way `stream_json_pretty` already does via `element_gap_ok_at(pos, ..)` + `value_at(pos)` (#1803). After #2578 the redundant asks are cache hits, so what is left to recover is the `rank1` + call overhead per repeat — small next to the per-node work the walk actually does (`value_at` scalar parsing, `IndexMap::insert`, one `String` per key from `resolve_display_key`).

**Plan:**
1. Measure deterministically first, on `terminus` (7950X, valgrind) — this is an attribution question, and `Ir` answers it without an interleaved run. Fixtures: `succinctly json generate 10mb -p users -s 20260101` (and `-p arrays`), plus the YAML twin via `succinctly yq`-readable generation or `yq -P` of the same file. Queries: `sort_by(.age) | length` (the `_by` walk: `push_generic_document_validation_error` + `sort_key_generic`), `sort | length` (`to_owned_cursor` per element), `[.users[]] | length` (materialization only). Run `valgrind --tool=cachegrind` on each and `cg_annotate` the output; read the *inclusive* `Ir` of `JsonCursor::text_position` / `YamlCursor::text_position`, `BalancedParens::rank1`, `ib_select1_sequential` / `AdvancePositions::get`, and the self cost of `to_owned_cursor_at_depth` and `push_generic_document_validation_error`. Count calls (`--collect-jumps` is unnecessary; cachegrind's per-function call attribution is enough). The ratio (position-resolve `Ir`) / (total `Ir`) is the ceiling any fusion can win.
2. Decide by threshold: if the resolve family is under ~3% of total `Ir` on every row, close this as "re-measured, not worth a fusion pass" with the table in the closing comment and a one-line note in `docs/optimizations/select-scan.md` (which already carries #2578's numbers) so it is not re-raised. This is the expected outcome given the repeat cache.
3. If it is above that: fuse, following #1803's existing shape rather than inventing one. In `to_owned_cursor_at_depth` add a pre-resolved inner entry `to_owned_cursor_at_depth_at(cursor, pos: Option<usize>, depth)` that the array arm calls after its own single `text_position()`, using `element_gap_ok_at(pos, is_first)` and `value_at(pos)` (JSON) / the YAML equivalent instead of `element_gap_ok` + `value()`; the object arm passes the value position `key_delimiter_ok`/`value_delimiter_ok` already resolved. Mirror the same in `push_generic_document_validation_error` (it is documented as "`to_owned_cursor_at_depth`'s own traversal", so the two must stay in step — CLAUDE.md's duplicated-predicate rule). Keep `element_gap_ok` for the callers that only need the `bool`.
4. If step 3 happens, A/B it the benchmarking.md way: interleaved per repetition, 11 reps, `--control` floor, output identity gated against `/usr/bin/jq` and `yq`, on both boxes (x86 = `terminus` 7950X, ARM = the M4 Pro Mac mini). Rows: the three queries above at 2 MB and 10 MB, JSON and YAML, plus `.` identity and `keys_unsorted` as must-not-move holdouts (the identity path does not go through `to_owned_cursor_at_depth`; if it moves, the change reached something it should not have). Report the 2 MB → 10 MB curve, not one ratio.
5. Tests: no behaviour change either way. If step 3 lands, the existing #1677/#1803/#2211/#2243 delimiter/gap tests in `tests/jq_cli_tests.rs` and `tests/yq_cli_tests.rs` are the gate for the fused checks (`[1,,2]`, `{"a":1,}`, `[,]`, `{,}`, missing `:`), and `sort_by` over an undecodable element (`test_*_1755`/the `[{"a":2,"s":"\ud800"},...]` repro named in `key_elements_generic`'s doc) pins that the validation walk still raises. Run the full `--features cli` suite; note `cargo test --lib` misses `tests/*.rs`.
6. Docs: step 2's note either way; if a fusion lands, a short entry in `docs/optimizations/select-scan.md` next to #2578's, with the `Ir` table from step 1 and the A/B curve from step 4.

**Risks / open questions:**
- The fusion touches the one traversal every materialization shares; a mistake in the threaded `pos` shows up as a wrong delimiter verdict, not a crash — the negative tests in step 5 are the guard, and both formats must be exercised (the YAML cursor's `text_position` semantics for a wrapped sequence item differ from JSON's).
- `push_generic_document_validation_error` and `to_owned_cursor_at_depth` are documented as the same traversal; fusing one and not the other reopens the drift the #1803 comment warns about.
- Do not run the wall-clock A/B on the 100 KB defaults — process spawn dominates; ≥ 1 MB inputs only.

**Dependencies / related:** #2168 (closed; the origin, and its closing "worth re-measuring" note), #2578 (the seed + exact-repeat cache that already absorbed most of this), #2604 (moved `path`/`key`/`parent`/`getpath` off the walk), #2692 (moved `select`/`if`/`and`/`or`/`//`/`not` off it — not reflected in this issue's body), #1803 (`element_gap_ok_at`, the fusion pattern to copy), #2580 (YAML's `ib_select1_from` copy missed #2578's seed policy — if step 1 shows YAML probing where JSON hits the cache, that is the reason, and it is that issue's fix, not this one's). No open PR references #2640.

**Class:** Sonnet — the deliverable is a deterministic cachegrind attribution against a stated threshold, and the code reading above says the repeat cache has most likely already taken the win, so the probable outcome is "measured, close, note it". Only if the numbers say otherwise does this become a two-function fusion with a copy-the-precedent shape and the standard two-box A/B; if that branch is taken and it turns out to need judgment beyond #1803's pattern, escalate then rather than pre-assigning Opus to a measurement.

doc.title: yq: a metadata assignment nested under `as` (`.b as $x | .a line_comment = $x`) is refused; real yq applies it
doc.body:
## Summary

A yq metadata assignment (`line_comment =`, `style =`, `anchor =`, #798) is refused with an explicit error whenever it sits anywhere other than a top-level pipe stage. The most common shape that hits this is a variable binding feeding the right-hand side:

```
$ printf 'a: 1\nb: hi\n' | yq '.b as $x | .a line_comment = $x'
a: 1 # hi
b: hi
$ printf 'a: 1\nb: hi\n' | succinctly yq '.b as $x | .a line_comment = $x'
Error: metadata assignment (line_comment/style/anchor = ...) is only supported as a top-level pipe stage
```

Verified against pinned yq v4.53.3 and succinctly at `3a3e88140`. The same refusal covers a write inside a `reduce`/`foreach` body or a `def` body.

## Why it is refused today

`resolve_meta_assign_writes` (`src/bin/succinctly/yq_runner.rs`) runs *before* the real evaluation. It flattens the expression's top-level pipe stages, re-evaluates each earlier stage to reach the document the write sees, then evaluates `path(TARGET)` and the right-hand side against that document via `evaluate_input`. A write nested under `Expr::As` would need `$x` bound when its RHS is evaluated, and `evaluate_input` on the RHS alone has no binding. `count_meta_assigns` compares the total number of `MetaAssign` nodes with the number of top-level stages and reports the mismatch rather than letting the nested write silently no-op (the outcome #798's triage ruled out).

Recorded in `docs/compliance/yq/limitations.md` under "Metadata assignment (`PATH <slot> = value`): what `succinctly yq` refuses or drops".

## Possible directions

- Descend `Expr::As { source, body }` in the pre-pass: evaluate `source` against the current document, then evaluate the body's writes with the binding installed (the evaluator already has a scope mechanism for `as`; the pre-pass would need to enter it, or wrap the RHS as `SOURCE as $x | RHS` and evaluate that).
- Longer term, move the write out of the pre-pass entirely: have `eval_meta_assign` (`src/jq/eval.rs`) record `(path, slot, text)` into a thread-local drained by the runner, the way `alias_identity` threads state through a write. That removes the top-level restriction for every construct at once, but needs the ambient path prefix (the spine-2416 `with_path_base` machinery) to turn a stage-relative target into a document path.

## Notes

- Found while reviewing the #798 PR1 branch; the explicit error was added in that review's fixes.
- `.b as $x | (.a style = "double")` has a CLI test pinning the current refusal (`nested_metadata_assignment_is_refused_explicitly` in `tests/yq_cli_tests.rs`); update it deliberately when this lands.

doc.title: jq: scalar roots have no node identity — ADR-0024 option D (shared strings) tracking issue
doc.body:
**Severity: Low**

## Summary
#2889 derives jq's `jv_identical` from `Rc` storage identity, which `OwnedValue::Array`/`Object` have and `OwnedValue::String`/numbers do not. A scalar root bound by `. as $x` therefore has no identity, and every scalar embed row refuses where jq answers. This is ADR-0024's deferred option D (shared strings), tracked here so it does not stay buried in the ADR.

## Repro
```console
$ echo '"s"' | jq -c '. as $x | {k:.} | .k | path($x)'
[]
$ echo '"s"' | succinctly jq -c '. as $x | {k:.} | .k | path($x)'
jq: error (at <stdin>:0): Invalid path expression with result "s"
$ echo '5' | jq -c '. as $x | {k:.} | .k | path($x)'
[]
```
Note jq's own rule for strings is pointer equality too (`. as $x | "s" | path($x)` on `"s"` refuses in jq), so value equality is not an acceptable proxy — #2642 closed exactly that hole.

## Root cause
`src/jq/value.rs`: `OwnedValue::String(String)` and the numeric variants own their storage inline; `embed_table_push` (`src/jq/eval_generic.rs`) skips non-containers because there is no storage to share, and `OwnedValue::shares_storage_with` answers `false` for them.

## Why this is separate from #2889
A representation change (`Rc<str>` or an interned/ref-counted string in `OwnedValue`, and something for numbers) with its own layout, allocator and perf consequences — ADR-0024 lists it as option D, deferred, and #2889 recorded the scalar residual rather than attempting it.

## Suggested fix direction
Under ADR-0024's measurement procedure: an `Rc<str>`-backed `String` variant (and a shared representation for `NumberLiteral`) with the `unshared-containers`-style holdout, `size_of::<OwnedValue>()` pinned, and the same A/B corpus. If accepted, `embed_table_push` and `shares_storage_with` extend to the new variants with no other change. Rows pinned as `owned-embed-refuse-scalar-{string,number}-root` in the sweep's `REFUSE_ONLY` and in `test_owned_embed_rebuilt_copies_still_refuse_2889`.

Related: #2889, #2999, ADR-0024 (option D).

doc.title: jq: thin refcounted string for scalar node identity (ADR-0024 option D, after #3182's measurement)
doc.body:
**Severity: Low**

## Summary
#3182 built and measured ADR-0024's option D (a refcounted `OwnedValue::String` and `NumberLiteral` spelling, so a scalar root bound by `as` keeps jq's pointer identity through `{k:.} | .k`) and rejected it: +8% to +50% peak RSS on scalar-heavy rows, because `Rc<String>` boxes the 24-byte `String` header the base layout keeps inside the 32-byte enum slot (a 48-byte allocation per string), and `Rc<str>` -- +16 bytes per scalar -- makes `reduce .[] as $s (""; . + $s)` quadratic. The full table is in ADR-0024's "Option D result" section; the code is on `wip/3182-option-d-measured`.

This issue tracks the one representation that meets every constraint at once, so it is priced before anyone builds it again.

## The representation
A thin refcounted string, jq's own `jvp_string` shape: one allocation holding `[refcount | len | cap | bytes...]`, a thin pointer in the enum arm, `ptr_eq` for identity, and in-place append when the refcount is one (grow by reallocating at 2x, amortized linear, so the fold stays linear as it is today and in jq). Same for the number spelling, without the capacity.

## The price, known up front
- **+16 bytes of heap per scalar** (the header), on every string and every number literal, whether or not anything ever shares it. On ten-byte strings that is ~+33% of the per-element heap; on the 2M-int rows #3182 measured, the `Rc<str>` half alone read +12% to +34% peak RSS, so this is not obviously under ADR-0024's "no shape regresses beyond the holdout's band" bar either. Measure the same corpus (`~/wrk/bench-scratch/issue-3182`, the harness is `rss-ab.py` in the #3182 write-up) with the `unshared-strings` holdout before deciding.
- **`unsafe` in `src/jq`**, which has none today and whose #2889/#3177 soundness arguments cite that fact. The type would need its own module, Miri, and a review of every `&str` accessor.
- The embed-table lookup runs for every node while a bind is active (the `is_container` gate goes), measured neutral-to-+6% wall in #3182 on bind-heavy rows.

## What it buys
The `scalar-*` rows in `scripts/jq-bind-origin-oracle-sweep.sh` that jq answers and succinctly refuses (the safe direction): `{k:.} | .k | path($x)` on a scalar root, `[.] | path(.[0] | $x)`, `tostring`/`@text`/`tonumber`/`[.] | add` passthroughs. The bridged builtins (`ltrimstr`, `sub`, `abs`, `[.] | sort | .[0]`, the `def f` constant-pool twin) would stay refuse-only even then.

Related: #3182, #2889, #3177, ADR-0024 (option D result).

doc.title: jq: TrackedVar rebuilt-root fix (#2642) refuse-only residual — owned embed map for pass-through constructions
doc.body:
## Context

#2642 (fixed in this issue's own PR) adds `RootWitness`/`demote_rebuilt_markers`
(`src/jq/eval.rs`) so a root-bound `$x`'s `Origin::Snapshot` marker is demoted
to `Untracked` before crossing into the owned-value evaluator whenever it
isn't proven to name that call's own document node -- closing the
value-equality-only certification hole that let a rebuilt equal-valued copy
be wrongly admitted (`. as $x | {a:1} | ($x.a) = 9` used to write `{"a":9}`;
jq refuses).

The fix is refuse-only by construction (a marker is only ever demoted from
`Snapshot` to `Untracked`, never the reverse), which means it also demotes a
few shapes that real jq's own reference-counted `jv` keeps as the *same*
node without ever allocating a new container for it. These are documented,
accepted residuals, not new correctness gaps -- but they are real,
verified-live regressions from "accept" to "refuse" that #2642's own triage
plan explicitly scoped to a follow-up rather than this fix.

## 1. "Owned embed map" — a handful of constructions lose accepted status

```console
$ echo '{"a":1}' | jq -c '. as $x | [.] | .[0] | path($x)'
[]
$ echo '{"a":1}' | succinctly jq -c '. as $x | [.] | .[0] | path($x)'
jq: error (at <stdin>:0): Invalid path expression with result {"a":1}
```

Same for `{k:.} | .k | path($x)`, `. + {} | path($x)`, and the navigation
happening *inside* the same `path()` invocation the marker is referenced in
(`[.] | path(.[0] | $x)`). In each case jq's own `jv` for the embedded
position is literally the same allocation as `.` itself (array/object
construction increments a refcount rather than copying), so `jv_identical`
still recognizes it; succinctly's `OwnedValue`-cloning model has no
per-position "this embeds a document node" fact to check against.

Recovering this needs the generic evaluator to record, for a constructed
value, which of its positions embed a document node (and which document/id)
— an "owned embed map" alongside the existing per-binding `BindOrigin`
tracking (#2072). #2642's own triage plan named this "Out of scope, to file
at stage 4" and it's filed here per that plan.

## 2. `reduce empty as $i (.; .)` — zero iterations, but still demoted

```console
$ echo '{"a":1}' | jq -c '. as $x | reduce empty as $i (.; .) | path($x)'
[]
$ echo '{"a":1}' | succinctly jq -c '. as $x | reduce empty as $i (.; .) | path($x)'
jq: error (at <stdin>:0): Invalid path expression with result {"a":1}
```

jq's own `reduce` over an empty source returns `INIT` verbatim (no update
ever ran) — the exact same `jv` as `.`. succinctly's generic-evaluator
`reduce` handling treats its own result as an opaque, freshly-computed
`OwnedValue` regardless of whether zero iterations ran, so the funnel demotes
unconditionally (`RootWitness::Owned`) rather than recognizing the
degenerate zero-iteration case as a pass-through. This was found live while
verifying #2642's own fix against its triage plan's oracle table (which lists
this row alongside `first(.)`/`select(true)`/`try . catch 1` — all of which
*do* stay correctly accepted) — narrower in scope than item 1 above (a single
construct, not a whole class), but the same underlying "no per-position
embed-tracking" root cause.

## Suggested approach

Both items are the same underlying gap: the generic evaluator's own
constructors (`Expr::Array`, `Expr::Object`, `+`, `reduce`/`foreach`) need to
record, for their *result*, whether (and where) they're merely relaying an
already-tracked document node rather than allocating a new one — extending
`BindOrigin`-style tracking from "where a *binding* came from" to "where a
*constructed value's own position* came from." Given the funnel-crossing
mechanism #2642 already built (`RootWitness::of`), the natural integration
point is to let a constructor pass a *richer* witness than `Owned` when it
can prove a specific position is a pass-through, rather than collapsing
everything non-cursor to the same catch-all.

Related: #2642 (this issue's own fix), #2072 (the `BindOrigin` node-tracking
this builds on), #1466 (the original sibling-node fabrication class this and
#2642 both belong to).

Update after PR #2890's code review round: two more real bugs were found and
fixed directly in that PR (not deferred here):

- `reduce`/`foreach`'s own UPDATE/EXTRACT positions were a missed funnel
  site (both the eager `eval_single` arm and the streaming
  `each_foreach_generic` twin) — the exact #2642 bug survived through
  `. as $x | reduce (1) as $i ({a:1}; ($x.a) = 9)`. Now fixed
  (`RootWitness::Owned`, since the fold's own accumulator is never
  cursor-backed regardless of what the ambient cursor is).
- `try error($x) catch path($x)` was found to regress (a case that
  previously worked correctly) from an over-eager `Owned` demotion added
  during review, then reverted -- `error($x)` raises a marker's own value
  verbatim, and jq's catch handler runs against that same value, so this
  case needs to stay untouched by `demote_rebuilt_markers` (see the fix's
  own inline comments on `run_try_handler_generic`/`try_single_generic`).

**New item added to this issue's own scope** (found during the same
review round, same root cause as the "owned embed map" item already
here): the `OwnedIdentity`/#2072 machinery a `key`/`parent`/`path`/
`file_index`-reading sibling stage routes through
(`eval_owned_identity_stages`, `owned_identity_values`,
`try_path_context_absent_sink`) does not get #2642's fix at all --
a blanket `Owned` witness there cannot distinguish a genuine, unrebuilt
document node the identity tracker already knows about (`id.base`) from an
actual rebuild, and applying it broke a previously-correct write
(`.foo | . as $x | (parent, ($x.a = 9))`, a succinctly-only extension
since jq has no `parent` builtin, used to write through the sibling
`parent` read; blanket demotion made it wrongly refuse). Reverted to
pre-#2642 behavior (unfixed, not regressed) rather than attempting to
thread the identity tracker's own `id.base`/`id.ancestors` witness through
under time pressure.

Suggested approach for this item: derive `RootWitness::of(id.base.as_ref())`
when `id.ancestors.is_empty()` (the position genuinely is `id.base`'s own,
unrebuilt node) and fall back to `RootWitness::Owned` only when `ancestors`
is non-empty (a genuinely rebuilt/descended value) -- the same distinction
the "owned embed map" item above needs anyway, since `OwnedIdentity`
already tracks exactly this provenance for #2072's own purposes.
